critical_remarks.issue: The introduction lacks a clear statement on how this research will influence the field of digital health interventions.
critical_remarks.impact: This affects the clarity of the research's contribution to the field.

critical_remarks.issue: The discussion section does not thoroughly explore the broader implications of the findings beyond BMI estimation.
critical_remarks.impact: This limits the understanding of the potential impact of the research.

critical_remarks.issue: The practical applications of the research could be more explicitly linked to real-world scenarios and benefits.
critical_remarks.impact: This reduces the clarity on how the research can be practically implemented.

improvement_suggestions.original_text: Recent computer vision-based approaches for BMI estimation have predominantly been limited to datasets of up to 7,211 full-body images or 14,500 facial images.
improvement_suggestions.improved_version: Current computer vision-based BMI estimation approaches have primarily utilized datasets with a maximum of 7,211 full-body images or 14,500 facial images.
improvement_suggestions.explanation: Clarifies the sentence structure for better readability and comprehension.

improvement_suggestions.original_text: We achieve a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 8% on our hold-out test dataset (real-world data only), using full-torso images.
improvement_suggestions.improved_version: Our model achieves an 8% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) on the hold-out test dataset, utilizing full-torso images.
improvement_suggestions.explanation: Enhances clarity and conciseness in presenting the research findings.

improvement_suggestions.original_text: To address the gap in datasets of limited size, we train deep learning models on a large-scale, real-world dataset of over 84,000 full-body images of 25,353 individuals.
improvement_suggestions.improved_version: To bridge the gap in small datasets, we utilize deep learning models trained on a comprehensive real-world dataset comprising over 84,000 full-body images from 25,353 individuals.
improvement_suggestions.explanation: Provides a more descriptive and engaging presentation of the dataset size and research approach.

improvement_suggestions.original_text: Our model demonstrates strong generalizability to unseen data, as demonstrated by our evaluation on the full-body Visual-Body-To-BMI dataset, achieving a MAPE of 13.38%, despite not being trained on this dataset at all.
improvement_suggestions.improved_version: Our model exhibits robust generalizability to unseen data, exemplified by achieving a MAPE of 13.38% on the Visual-Body-To-BMI dataset, despite not being trained on this specific dataset.
improvement_suggestions.explanation: Enhances the emphasis on the model's generalizability and performance on unseen data.

improvement_suggestions.original_text: Our work also provides insights for remote weight estimation during telemedicine consultations.
improvement_suggestions.improved_version: Additionally, our research offers valuable insights for remote weight estimation in telemedicine consultations.
improvement_suggestions.explanation: Strengthens the statement on the practical implications of the research.

detailed_feedback.field_influence: The research presents a significant contribution to the field of digital health interventions by introducing a novel approach to BMI estimation from smartphone images using deep learning on a large-scale real-world dataset.
detailed_feedback.broader_implications: The findings have broader implications for telehealth services, emergency medical scenarios, and remote health monitoring, offering a digital, real-time solution for weight assessment.
detailed_feedback.future_research_impact: The study's focus on different image perspectives and the evaluation on external datasets pave the way for future research on optimizing BMI estimation models for diverse applications and datasets.
detailed_feedback.practical_applications: The research showcases practical applications in image filtering, BMI estimation, and mobile deployment, demonstrating the potential for real-world implementation in healthcare settings.
detailed_feedback.policy_implications: The study's findings can inform policies related to digital health interventions, telemedicine, and remote monitoring, highlighting the importance of accurate and efficient weight estimation methods.

summary: The research demonstrates a significant contribution to the field of digital health interventions through innovative BMI estimation from smartphone images. While the study presents valuable insights and practical applications, improvements are needed in clearly articulating the field influence, broader implications, and practical relevance of the findings.
